properties.name: WHAT WORKED, re-measured on 0.77.0 (2026-10-02): `--call create_edges` with "check_only": true validates the batch and writes nothing. The export content_hash was unchanged afterwards, and a bad item is listed with its index. Do not regress it. Note for door agents: a failing check exits 0, so the verdict is would_apply, not the exit code
properties.statement:
From the "Measured" table of art:vscode-call-door-field-report-2026-10-02 ("--call create_edges with check_only: true validates the batch and writes nothing"), and the pattern "check_only for an edge batch". Re-measured by triage agent D (0.77.0, scratch store g110; outputs triage-D/out/create_edges_check*.stdout).

- A valid one-edge batch (SATISFIES cap:c0 → req:r5) with check_only: exit 0, {applied:false, check_only:true, checked:1, failures:[], would_apply:true, note:"every item validated; send the same batch without check_only to write it"}.
- A two-edge batch, one with edge_type NOT_A_RELATION: exit 0, {applied:false, checked:2, failures:[{index:1, id:"NOT_A_RELATION cap:c1 -> req:r5", error:"Unknown edge type: NOT_A_RELATION"}], would_apply:false}, with a note that a bulk write is all or nothing.
- Nothing written: export_graph afterwards still had 140 edges, and its content_hash equals the export taken before the checks (sha256:99a78218…85f0).

HOLDS. For a door agent, would_apply is the verdict, because a failed check still exits 0.
